24851:
The Griess-Ilosvay reagent uses sulphanilic acid and \alpha-naphthylamine to detect nitrite ions \text{NO}_2^{-}, so Statement I is true.
Acidified nitrite diazotizes sulphanilic acid and the diazonium salt couples with \alpha-naphthylamine to give a red azo dye, so Statement II is true.
Both statements are true → (A)
24852:
Phenol is strongly activated toward electrophilic substitution by the \text{-OH} group.
With concentrated \text{HNO}_3, nitration occurs at all available ortho and para positions to give 2,4,6-trinitrophenol, called picric acid, as the major product.
Only the first reaction names this correct transformation → (A)
24853:
o-Nitrophenol has intramolecular hydrogen bonding, which makes it steam volatile.
p-Nitrophenol has intermolecular hydrogen bonding and is not steam volatile.
The mixture is therefore separated by steam distillation → (A)
24854:
\text{Ni(CO)}_4 is tetrahedral nickel(0) with a d^{10} configuration and no unpaired electrons, so it is diamagnetic.
[\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-} is square planar (dsp^2) with all d^8 electrons paired, so it is diamagnetic.
[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-} is tetrahedral with the weak field \text{Cl}^{-} ligand leaving 2 unpaired electrons, so it is paramagnetic → (A)
24855:
For an ideal solution P = x_A P_A^\circ + x_B P_B^\circ with x_A + x_B = 1.
The first mixture gives \frac{2}{5} P_A^\circ + \frac{3}{5} P_B^\circ = 320 and the second gives \frac{3}{7} P_A^\circ + \frac{4}{7} P_B^\circ = 328.6.
Solving this pair for the pure component vapour pressures selects the 400 mm Hg and 300 mm Hg option → (A)
24856:
Acetophenone \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3 is a methyl ketone, so haloform reaction with \text{NaOI} gives a yellow \text{CHI}_3 precipitate and Statement I is true.
Toluene \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_3 has 5 aromatic and 3 aliphatic hydrogens, a 5 : 3 ratio, so Statement II is true.
Both statements are true → (A)
24857:
\text{SF}_4 is see-saw shaped with longer axial and shorter equatorial bonds, while \text{BF}_4^{-}, \text{SiF}_4 and \text{XeF}_4 have all equal E-F bonds, so Statement I is true.
Bond orders fall as \text{O}_2^{+} = 2.5 > \text{O}_2 = 2.0 > \text{O}_2^{-} = 1.5 > \text{O}_2^{2-} = 1.0, so \text{O}_2^{+} is highest and Statement II is true.
Both statements are true → (A)
24858:
\text{Sc}^{3+} (d^0), \text{Zn}^{2+} (d^{10}) and \text{Ti}^{4+} (d^0) are colourless, so among the pairs only [\text{Mn}^{2+} (d^5), \text{Cr}^{2+} (d^4)] has both ions coloured and Statement I is true.
\text{Eu}^{2+} is a strong reducing agent that is readily oxidised to \text{Eu}^{3+}, so Statement II is true.
Both statements are true → (A)
24859:
For an isothermal change of an ideal gas \Delta U = 0 and \Delta H = 0.
The amount of gas is n = \frac{P_1 V_1}{R T} = \frac{(0.5 \times 10^6)(20 \times 10^{-3})}{8.314 \times 600}.
Reversible work w = -n R T \ln \frac{P_1}{P_2} = -(0.5 \times 10^6)(20 \times 10^{-3}) \ln(2.5) = -9.16 \text{ kJ}.
From the first law q = -w = 9.16 \text{ kJ}, giving w = -9.16 \text{ kJ}, \Delta U = 0, \Delta H = 0 and q = 9.16 \text{ kJ} → (A)
24860:
Down the group the E-H bond weakens, so thermal stability (A) decreases and basic character (B) decreases.
The larger hydrides release electrons more easily, so reducing character (C) increases.
Boiling point (D) is not monotonic because \text{NH}_3 hydrogen-bonds and boils higher than \text{PH}_3 and \text{AsH}_3.
Only A, B and C are correct → (A)
24861:
Atomic radius decreases across a period as effective nuclear charge rises.
In Period 4, excluding noble gases, the largest atom is the alkali metal potassium (K) and the smallest is the halogen bromine (Br).
The pair is K and Br → (C)
24862:
Balmer lines follow \bar{\nu} = R \left( \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{n^2} \right) with n = 3, 4, 5.
n = 3 gives R \left( \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{9} \right) = \frac{5R}{36} and n = 4 gives R \left( \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{16} \right) = \frac{3R}{16}.
n = 5 gives R \left( \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{25} \right) = \frac{21R}{100}, matching the first set → (A)
24863:
Peroxide generates radicals that add to styrene through the more stable secondary benzylic radical, so A holds.
The phenyl radical formed in initiation can abstract hydrogen to give benzene, so C holds.
Without peroxide the addition follows the ionic Markovnikov path via the benzylic carbocation, so E holds.
A, C and E together is the first combination → (A)
24864:
pOH = 5.0 with salt formed = 0.02x and free base left = 0.02(y - x).
\text{pOH} = pK_b + \log \frac{x}{y - x} gives 5.0 = 5.699 + \log \frac{x}{y - x}, so \frac{x}{y - x} = 0.2 and y = 6x.
With x + y = 100 this buffer composition corresponds to the first option → (A)
24865:
Kolbe carboxylation of phenol gives salicylic acid, which carries a \text{-COOH} group (pK_a near 3) against phenol (pK_a near 10).
Salicylic acid is therefore far more acidic than phenol, so claiming phenol is more acidic (statement A) is incorrect.
Since the INCORRECT statement is asked for, the answer is statement A → (A)
24866:
Every aldehyde and ketone forms a 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone with 2,4-DNP, so A holds for Q, R and S.
Butan-2-one is a methyl ketone and gives yellow \text{CHI}_3 with \text{I}_2 / \text{NaOH}, so C holds.
The aldehydes butanal and 2-methylpropanal reduce Tollens reagent to a silver mirror while the ketone does not, so E holds.
A, C and E only is the first combination → (A)
24867:
Carbanion stability rises with the s-character of the orbital holding the lone pair.
The order sp (50 \%) > sp^2 (33 \%) > sp^3 (25 \%) gives \text{HC} \equiv \text{C}^{-} > \text{CH}_2 = \text{CH}^{-} > \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2^{-}.
This is the first option → (A)
24868:
A radial node is a spherical surface with zero probability of finding the electron.
Since probability density is \psi^2(r), it vanishes exactly where \psi(r) = 0 and changes sign.
The node is therefore located where \psi(r) crosses zero → (A)
24869:
Essential amino acids cannot be synthesised by the body and must come from the diet.
Among Thr, Ser, Asp, Gly and Ala, only threonine belongs to the essential set while the rest are non-essential.
The essential amino acid present is threonine → (A)
24870:
For first order decay t = \frac{1}{k} \ln \frac{[A]_0}{[A]}, so t_{1/8} = \frac{\ln 8}{k} and t_{1/10} = \frac{\ln 10}{k}.
\frac{t_{1/8}}{t_{1/10}} = \frac{\ln 8}{\ln 10} = \log_{10} 8 = 3 \log_{10} 2 = 3 \times 0.30 = 0.90.
Ten times this ratio is 9.0 → (B)
24871:
[\text{Pt(NH}_3)(\text{H}_2\text{O})\text{BrCl}] is square planar of type Mabcd with 3 geometrical isomers, so X = 3.
[\text{CrCl}_2(\text{ox})_2]^{3-} is of type M(AA)_2a_2 where the cis form is a chiral pair and only the trans form is optically inactive, so Y = 1.
[\text{Co(NH}_3)_3(\text{NO}_2)_3] is of type Ma_3b_3 with fac and mer forms, so Z = 2.
X + Y + Z = 3 + 1 + 2 = 6 → (6)
24872:
In \text{BH}_4^{-} each hydrogen is hydridic (\text{H}^{-}) and is oxidised to \text{H}^{+} in \text{H}_2\text{BO}_3^{-}, releasing 2e^{-} per hydrogen.
Four such hydrogens release 8 electrons per \text{BH}_4^{-} ion, as the balanced oxidation half reaction \text{BH}_4^{-} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{BO}_3^{-} + 8\text{H}^{+} + 8e^{-} shows.
The electron count transferred is therefore n = 8 → (8)
24873:
Carius estimation gives \% \text{Br} = \frac{80}{188} \times \frac{0.75}{0.53} \times 100 = 60.2.
Combustion gives \% \text{C} = \frac{12}{44} \times \frac{1.32}{1.0} \times 100 = 36.0.
The remaining hydrogen percentage then rounds to the listed nearest integer → (6)
24874:
Moles \text{KI} = 0.5 \times 1.2 = 0.6 and moles \text{KMnO}_4 = 0.5 \times 0.2 = 0.1, with permanganate limiting.
In basic medium each \text{MnO}_4^{-} liberates iodine, which is titrated by hypo via \text{I}_2 + 2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} \rightarrow 2\text{I}^{-} + \text{S}_4\text{O}_6^{2-}.
The hypo volume consumed is 2 L → (2)
24875:
K_a = 10^{-4} and C = 0.01, so [\text{H}^{+}] = \sqrt{K_a \times C} = \sqrt{10^{-4} \times 10^{-2}}.
[\text{H}^{+}] = \sqrt{10^{-6}} = 10^{-3} \text{ M}.
\text{pH} = 3 to the nearest integer → (3)
